answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can gate its marketplace inlet with a refundable stake: each new identity locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught running duplicate personas. Honest agents recover the stake plus reputation over time, while an attacker spawning thousands of clones must fund every one, so attack cost scales linearly. Like a zephyr bending only the tallest reeds, the rule does not block newcomers outright; it makes fakery expensive and turns the market into a haven where one verified history is worth more than a thousand cheap masks.
